fullPassage: A rhyme is usually the repetition of the final sound of a word. Most often, it is consciously used for a musical effect in the final position of lines within poems or songs. Let’s look at three ways that rhyme is used in rap lyrics. First, if two lines finish with words that rhyme, this is called an end rhyme, which is the most representative kind of rhyme. Try reading the following example aloud. My house is so big you cannot see the top Don’t jump off the roof that is quite a long drop The two rhyming words “top” and “drop” share an ending sound “op.” Second, words can rhyme within the same line. This creates an internal rhyme, which involves a word in the middle of a line and another word in the same or the next line. For example, They’re never gonna learn how to wait their turn Third, rappers often use imperfect rhymes. For example, “start,” “sport,” and “straight” do not exactly rhyme, but they create a pattern of similar sounds /s/ and /t/. In most imperfect rhymes, the consonants are identical while the vowel sounds are different, or the other way round. When a sequence of rhymed words is spoken aloud, it creates a rhythmic pattern or “flow.” This helps the song keep a steady beat, pleases the ear, and evokes emotions. So, if you create a rap, rhyming is a great way to make your voice stronger and reach your listeners. ‘start’, ‘sport’,
